root_cause.text: The error handling in vfio_pci_core_feature_dma_buf() incorrectly falls through to the generic unwind chain (including vfio_device_put_registration and freeing physical objects) after dma_buf_fd() fails, even though when dma_buf_export() succeeded only dma_buf_put() should be called, leading to an unbalanced refcount and double free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes the error path from jumping to `err_dma_buf` (which calls `dma_buf_put`) and then falling through to `err_dev_put` and `err_free_phys`, to performing only `dma_buf_put` and immediately returning the error. The commit description confirms: “ignores its own advice to only use dma_buf_put() after dma_buf_export(), instead falling through the entire unwind chain” and that this “can result in an unbalanced refcount on the vfio device and double free of allocated objects.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The function vfio_pci_core_feature_dma_buf() in this commit has an incorrect error handling path after dma_buf_fd() fails. When dma_buf_fd() returns an error, the code goes to err_dma_buf which calls dma_buf_put(), but then falls through to err_dev_put which calls vfio_device_put_registration(), and then kfree of priv->phys_vec and priv. However, dma_buf_put() will eventually trigger the release callback that frees these resources and drops the registration reference, leading to double free and unbalanced refcount. The correct fix should skip the extra cleanup after dma_buf_put().
